title: Summary statistics of a list of numbers
prompt:
Read lines from standard input, each holding one decimal number: an optional minus sign, one or more digits, and optionally a `.` followed by one or more digits (`12`, `-3.5`, `0.25`; no exponent, no plus sign, nothing like `.5` or `5.`). Spaces at the start and end of a line are ignored, and blank lines are skipped. Any other line prints `line N: not a number` (N counts the lines from 1) and is otherwise ignored.

If at least one number was read, print five lines:
`count=N`
`mean=M` (the sum of the numbers added in input order, divided by the count)
`median=D` (the middle value after sorting, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even)
`stddev=S` (the population standard deviation: the square root of the mean of the squared differences from the mean)
`range=LO..HI` (the smallest and the largest number)
All of them except the count are written with exactly 3 digits after the decimal point, rounded to the nearest. If no number was read print `no data`. Every answer in the tests is well away from a rounding tie.

cases.name: example
cases.expected_output:
line 3: not a number
count=7
mean=15.393

stddev=13.233
range=-1.000..42.250
